authoredSolutions.1: Inside a long current-carrying solenoid the magnetic field \(\overrightarrow{B}\) is directed along the axis. The electron is projected along the same axis, so \(\overrightarrow{v}\parallel\overrightarrow{B}\) and the magnetic force \(\overrightarrow{F}=-e\left(\overrightarrow{v}\times\overrightarrow{B}\right)=0\). With no force acting on it, the electron continues to move with uniform velocity along the axis, so the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.2: For a plane electromagnetic wave \(\overrightarrow{E}\), \(\overrightarrow{B}\) and the direction of propagation form a right-handed triad, with \(B_{0}=\dfrac{E_{0}}{c}\). The phase \(\omega\left(t-\dfrac{z}{c}\right)\) shows propagation along \(+\widehat{k}\), and \(\overrightarrow{E}\) is along \(\widehat{i}\). Since \(\widehat{i}\times\widehat{j}=\widehat{k}\), the magnetic field must lie along \(\widehat{j}\): \[\overrightarrow{B}=\widehat{j}\,\frac{40}{c}\cos\omega\left(t-\frac{z}{c}\right).\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.3: For \(\ _{0}^{1}n+\ _{92}^{235}U\) the totals to be conserved are \(Z=92\) and \(A=236\). Option D gives \(Z=56+36=92\) and \(A=144+89+3\times1=236\), so it balances. authoredSolutions.4: The lens equation is \(\dfrac{1}{f}=\dfrac{1}{v}-\dfrac{1}{u}\). Differentiating, \[-\frac{df}{f^{2}}=-\frac{dv}{v^{2}}+\frac{du}{u^{2}}.\] Adding the magnitudes of the individual contributions for the maximum error, \[\Delta f=f^{2}\left\lbrack\frac{\Delta u}{u^{2}}+\frac{\Delta v}{v^{2}}\right\rbrack.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.5: Statement I: with the liquid everywhere at rest, Bernoulli's equation gives \(P_{1}+\rho gh_{1}=P_{2}+\rho gh_{2}\), i.e. \(P_{1}-P_{2}=\rho g\left(h_{2}-h_{1}\right)\), so Statement I is correct. Statement II: in the venturi tube of the figure \(v_{1}\) is the speed in the wide section and \(v_{2}\) the speed in the throat, and Bernoulli's equation along the horizontal axis gives \(P_{1}-P_{2}=\rho gh=\dfrac{1}{2}\rho\left(v_{2}^{2}-v_{1}^{2}\right)\), i.e. \(2gh=v_{2}^{2}-v_{1}^{2}\). The printed relation \(2gh=v_{1}^{2}-v_{2}^{2}\) has the terms interchanged, so Statement II is incorrect. The correct choice is D.
